q: The actual (dressed) width of solid lumber is less than its nominal size by about how many millimeters?
n: Surfacing removes roughly 1/2" (about 12 mm) from the nominal size.

q: For preliminary design, what is the recommended maximum span of a solid wood beam?
n: Solid sawn beams are practical up to about 6 m; longer spans call for glulam or steel.

q: Which wood is known as Philippine ebony?
n: Kamagong is the native ebony.

q: In the Philippines, lumber is commonly sold in what lengths?
n: Local lumber comes in 8', 10', 12' and so on.

q: Which of these is also called chipboard?
n: Chipboard is particle board.

q: What are the wooden strips laid on a concrete slab to fasten a subfloor or wood flooring to?
n: Sleepers give a nailing base over concrete.

q: What protects engineered wood from moisture?
n: Sealing the edges and faces keeps moisture out of the core.

q: What is laid on the slab before installing wood flooring?
n: An underlayment cushions and blocks moisture under the floor.

q: What does S2S stand for in lumber?
n: S2S lumber is planed on two faces.

q: What is the heavy horizontal timber at the bottom of a wood frame, resting on the foundation?
n: The sill plate is anchored to the foundation.

q: Conifers are classified as what kind of wood?
n: Conifers (pines, firs) are softwoods.

q: Which wood is known as Philippine mahogany?
n: Tanguile (and lauan) are sold as Philippine mahogany.

q: Which wood is commonly used for door frames for its strength and durability?
n: Yakal is a dense, durable structural hardwood.

q: Which native Philippine tree is known for its dense, durable hardwood?
n: Narra is native; mahogany and pine are introduced.

q: What is undressed lumber called?
n: Rough lumber has not been planed.

q: Commercial lumber in the Philippines is usually sold in what kind of lengths?
n: Stock lengths are even numbers of feet.

q: Where is coco lumber least commonly used?
n: Coco lumber is hard to machine to fine profiles like jambs.

q: What is the main reason for seasoning lumber before use?
o: To reduce moisture content and prevent warping
n: Dry lumber is stable and stronger.

q: How many board feet are in 250 pieces of 2" × 3" × 10' lumber?
What is the general term for baseboards, cornices, balusters and similar detailed wood elements?
n: Millwork is milled wood trim and fittings.

q: Which of these is NOT millwork?
n: Millwork is wood; steel railings are metalwork.

q: Which item in this list is NOT millwork?
n: Light reflectors are fixtures, not milled wood.

q: Which of these is millwork?
n: A wood cornice is millwork.

q: Which item in this list counts as millwork?
n: A wood dresser is millwork.

q: What connector joins members in wood trusses?
n: Gusset plates (wood or metal) join truss members.

q: Where are gang nails typically used?
n: Gang-nail plates join timber truss members.

q: What adhesive is used to stick a wood board to concrete?
n: Construction adhesive ("liquid nail") bonds wood to masonry.

q: Why must a board be positioned accurately when using liquid nail?
o: It is hard to correct once it has dried
n: Once cured it is difficult to reposition.

q: How would you install 3/4" plywood over an uneven surface?
n: A leveled frame bridges the unevenness.

q: What is the vernacular term for a wood joist?
n: Soleras is the local term for joists (floor beams).

q: What is the vernacular term for a rabbet joint?
n: Canto mesa is the rabbet (rebate).

q: What tool is used to turn a baluster?
n: A torno is a lathe.

q: What is the vernacular term for the wood molding at the bottom of a wall?
n: Rodapis is the baseboard.

q: What is the vernacular term for the horizontal member at the top or bottom of a wall frame?
n: Soleras also names the sill/top plate in local usage.

q: What is the structural support of a stair called?
n: Stringers carry the treads and risers.

q: What post is located at the end of a stair run and anchors the handrail?
n: Newel posts stand at the start, end and turns of a stair.

q: What is the vertical part between two treads?
n: The riser closes the space between treads.

q: What is the most suitable joint for wood flooring?
n: Tongue-and-groove boards interlock.

q: Which joint is typically used for the back panel of a cabinet?
n: The back panel sits in a rabbet cut into the carcass.

q: Which joint is commonly used at countertop corners?
n: Countertop corners are mitered.

q: Which joint gives interlocking strength and is often used at drawer corners?
n: Dovetails resist pulling apart.

q: What do you call a light circular saw on a spring-loaded pivoting arm over a metal base?
n: A chop (miter) saw pivots down onto the work.

q: Which power tool shapes and finishes wood with a continuous abrasive loop?
n: Belt sanders remove material fast.

q: Which saw uses a reciprocating blade to cut irregular curves?
n: A jigsaw cuts curves.

q: Which saw cuts various materials and can be either handheld or table-mounted?
n: Circular saws come in handheld and mounted forms.

q: What is a circular saw mounted under a table, with the work pushed across it?
n: The blade projects through the table top.
